chore(cpp): join the two integration lines of the C++ gateway (stage 2a with stage 1) and add the reduced-confinement fallback (stage X)

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `agent-jobs/cppgw-integrate-s2a-20261118-44264106398-1` of ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi: a known-good state of `cpp/gateway/`, a C++20 port of this repository's TypeScript gateway (`src/`, `serve.ts`), with a JavaScript-style runtime layer (`include/uos/rt`, `src/rt`, `src/runtime`), vendored simdjson and simdutf (`cpp/gateway/third_party/`), ICU for Unicode, and about 442 standalone test binaries (`cpp/gateway/tests/**/*_test.cpp`). On this state the release build passes its whole suite on Linux ARM64. The native gateway is already 1.2-1.9x faster than the TypeScript gateway on Bun end to end and uses about a third of the memory (`cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-perf-request-path-20261117.md`). Every deployment target is 64-bit ARM: an Arch Linux ARM VPS, an Apple Silicon Mac and a Raspberry Pi.

OWNER POLICY (binding): generic functionality comes from mature open-source or standard libraries; exact parity with Bun's quirks and error wording is NOT required; less first-party code is preferred. What must hold: the gateway's functional behaviour (wire formats, status codes, stored data, authentication and validation decisions, accounting) and security never getting weaker.

READ FIRST: `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` (portable build-and-test driver; invoke it as `bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh ...`, the file lacks its executable bit), `cpp/gateway/docs/BUILD.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/RUNTIME.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/OSS-REPLACEMENT-PLAN.md`, `cpp/gateway/PORTING.md` (its coroutine rules are mandatory; its "Host safety" and "compile only through tools/unit.sh" rules apply to the authors' server, not to your disposable runner; where it demands exact Bun parity, the owner policy above wins). `python3 cpp/gateway/tools/links.py <test>` prints a test's application sources; every `src/rt/*.cpp` and the vendored libraries link into every test.

About ten other agents are changing other parts of `cpp/gateway` on their own branches at the same time (URL, HTTP parsing, regex, WebSocket, passkey CBOR and ASN.1, BigInt, date/console/filesystem/env/headers helpers, the stored-value reader, a test-suite repair). You are an INTEGRATOR (see TASK); keep your own edits to what integration needs.

GENERAL RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Run tests with an empty `HOME`, a fresh `TMPDIR` and no provider variables. No real provider traffic: use local mocks only.
- Do not edit `.github/` (unless your task says so), the TypeScript, or `cpp/` outside `cpp/gateway/`. Do not delete or weaken tests.
- Model connections can drop: create your report file in the first minutes and commit small steps often (the tree must build at each commit). Leave no build output, binaries or downloads in the checkout.
- Report file: `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/<job id>.md`: what you did, exact commands, real counts and measurements, what is unfinished, defects found outside your paths (report, do not fix). End your final message with the same summary.

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner (Ubuntu 24.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network). Its packages are too old for this tree: install Clang 21 or newer from apt.llvm.org (or GCC 14+), build Boost 1.92.0 `json` and `container` static libraries from the official source archive in a temp directory (the tree needs Boost >= 1.86), install OpenSSL 3, zlib, ICU, brotli, zstd development packages and build SQLite 3.54.0 as `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` describes. Bun 1.4.0 may be installed when you need to run the TypeScript.

OWNED PATHS
- anything under `cpp/gateway/` and `.github/workflows/cpp-gateway-*.yml` that the integration needs. Not the TypeScript; vendored sources under `cpp/gateway/third_party/` stay byte-identical.

TASK
Two integration lines of this port diverged about a day ago and both are green on ARM64:
  LINE A (your starting branch, `agent-jobs/cppgw-integrate-s2a-20261118-44264106398-1`, report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-integrate-s2a-20261118.md`): the port head with the hand-written JSON parser deleted (simdjson only), simdutf UTF conversion, the central input-limits header, a faster large-body path, the unified CI workflow, cheaper log records, Boost.Beast outbound WebSocket, ICU case mapping/collation, macOS and Raspberry Pi packaging, operator kit. 443 binaries, 5,039 cases.
  LINE B stage 1 (`agent-jobs/cppgw-integrate-s1-c1-44247790145-1`, report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-integrate-s1-20261118.md`): branched from an OLDER commit (before the JSON deletion): date/console/filesystem/environment/Headers helpers on the standard library, ICU case mapping/collation (the same change line A has), HTTP server request parsing on llhttp (vendors `third_party/llhttp`). 443 binaries, 5,037 cases.
Merge LINE B stage 1 into your branch with an ordinary `git merge` commit, then merge `agent-jobs/cppgw-landlock-fallback-c1-44247790145-1` (opt-in reduced Landlock confinement for kernels older than 7.0; it was branched from line A's ancestor, so it should merge cleanly; security-sensitive: the default policy and the seccomp filter must stay byte-identical to what that branch has).
This is the hard cross-line merge: expect real conflicts wherever line A changed files after the divergence that line B also changed: `src/rt/string.cpp` (both have the ICU change: keep ONE copy of it plus line A's simdutf UTF conversion), `src/rt/json.cpp` and its users (line A deleted the hand-written parser: keep the deletion; adapt any line-B code that still calls removed JSON functions), `src/rt/console.cpp`, `fs.cpp`, `env.cpp`, `headers.cpp`, `date.cpp` (line B rewrote them: keep line B's versions and re-apply any line-A change that touched them, for example the input limits), `src/runtime/http.cpp` (line B: llhttp request parsing; line A: other edits), tests of those components, and the shared registries (`fuzz/targets.json`, `docs/DEVIATIONS-FROM-BUN.md`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `tools/vendor_sources.py`, `cmake/vendors.json`, `tests/LINKS.txt`, `docs/CI.md`, `cmake/ci/driver.py`). Resolve every conflict keeping BOTH lines' intent; never resolve by dropping one side's change; when two versions of the same test expectation differ, the one consistent with the merged code and the owner policy wins, and say so in the commit message.
Then make every build path work and run the whole suite: release configuration, all four shards, then the `asan` configuration for the files that had conflicts, until everything is green on your ARM64 runner.
Work fast and in this order: merge, resolve, build, fix compile errors, run shard 1, fix, run the rest. Commit after each of those steps. Write `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-integrate-x1-20261118.md`: every conflicted file and how it was resolved, test decisions, final counts per shard.

DONE WHEN
`bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh --config release --shard N/4` passes for N = 1..4 with zero failing binaries on your ARM64 runner, `git log` shows the two merges, and the report lists every conflicted file with its resolution. The maintainer will merge the remaining line-B branches onto your result.
